NO TICKET YET
The app cannot tell a stopped service from a stopped environment
`pdsm stop` stops the services inside the container; the proot environment keeps running. The app has one runtime signal — an HTTP ping to
/home with a 1.5 s timeout — so "services down, proot alive" and "everything down" are the same observable state, and both render as OFFLINE.
The consequence is not cosmetic: LibraryActivity.canStartServer() reads "not answering" as "nothing is running", so Retry can start a SECOND
proot over a live one — the collision class ADR-4832 documents (shared /tmp, /dev/shm, ports). Reachable after any app restart, because the
handle that would have stopped the first one is a field on an Activity-scoped ServerController.
The environment already tells us it exited — startEnvironment's onProcessExit only logs it. Nothing kills the proot when the app closes.
Detection exists and is tested (EnvironmentProcess). Wiring it needs: the handle per process, "ensure up" not "start", and a boot grace.
CARRIED, NOT BLOCKING
Found in the last two days; recorded so they are met on purpose
The Books "downloads" link is the last fragment hosting itself. Needs an index that can be opened with nothing in flight.
No run-level disk budget. Ten places read free space by hand, so there is nowhere to put one.
The three live REST streams can still start together: one provisioner drains asynchronously, so the others see no session yet.
Books reports no transfer rate; the maps card cannot show "adding content" because its progress belongs to the module queue.
Sessions do not survive process death (ADFA-4874), so a download measured in hours has no durable record.
Order: 5061 first, 4954 alongside it (done), then 5074 (done), then 5062. 5074 came before 5062 because 5062 migrates the
SetupProgressActivity key switch — work thrown away if the hosting changed after it.
4758 can run whenever and reads better after 5061; do not close it as superseded, it is the one that can lose a user's content.
The canvas is not page-sized on purpose. Grow it when something new belongs here rather than dropping an item to make room.
